question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=2-\frac{1}{k}\sqrt[3]{2x+4}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=2-\frac{1}{k}\sqrt[3]{2y+4}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2-\frac{1}{k}\sqrt[3]{2y+4} \\ \frac{1}{k}\sqrt[3]{2y+4} & =2-x \\ \sqrt[3]{2y+4} & =k(2-x) \\ {(\sqrt[3]{2y+4})}^{3} & ={(k(2-x))}^{3} \\ 2y+4 & ={k}^{3}(2-x)^{3} \\ 2y & ={k}^{3}(2-x)^{3}-4 \\ y & =\frac{{k}^{3}}{2}(2-x)^{3}-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{{k}^{3}}{2}(2-x)^{3}-2.
$$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{k}^{3}}{2}=32\,⟹\,k=4.
$$
